requirements.text: Open a Employee Profile Update HR service case under Talent Management to track it for account( ACC-PROMO-2024-SS) and assign to HR Service Desk
requirements.sql: SELECT COUNT(*) FROM hr_case WHERE hr_case_id = 61 AND hr_service = 35 AND opened_for = 12 AND coe_type = 'Talent Management' AND account_number = 'ACC-PROMO-2024-SS' AND assignment_group = 4 AND priority = 'moderate'
assumptions: id assumed next in sequence (61 after 60); the case number HRC0000771 is server-assigned, so the row is anchored by id
hr_service 35 is Employee Profile Update; assignment_group 4 is HR Service Desk
opened_for 12 is Samantha Stone's HR profile, the employee the case is about
priority not stated; the policy's default for a new case is moderate

requirements.text: Once everything's checked off, go ahead and close out the case directly
requirements.sql: SELECT COUNT(*) FROM hr_case WHERE hr_case_id = 61 AND status = 'closed_complete'
assumptions: closed_complete is the closing status in the policy's list of case statuses and the benchmark check's value; 'closed' is not in that list and may not be reached directly

requirements.sql: SELECT COUNT(*) FROM hr_case_task WHERE hr_case_task_id = 150 AND parent_case = 61 AND task_type = 'checklist' AND status = 'closed_complete'
assumptions: id assumed next in sequence (150 after 149)
status closed_complete implied by the request, not stated: every item is done and the case is closed, and the policy lets a case close only when its mandatory tasks are complete

requirements.text: with at least 3 items and mark them all done
requirements.sql: SELECT COUNT(*) FROM checklist WHERE case_task_id = 150 AND checked = 1
assumptions: several items are created in no stated order, so they are selected by their task, not by id
at least 3 items, so the count of checked items must exceed 2

requirements.sql: SELECT COUNT(*) FROM checklist WHERE case_task_id = 150 AND checked != 1
assumptions: no item of the checklist task may be left unchecked
disagreement: checked: A != 1, B 0; chose != 1 because it is the tighter predicate (any value other than done counts) and the two agree on the seed's values 0 and 1

requirements.sql: SELECT COUNT(*) FROM hr_profile WHERE hr_profile_id = 12 AND position = 'HR'

requirements.text: if not found create one titled 'Resolution Guide: Employee Promotion fulfillment steps for Talent Management position changes'

used_as not stated; the policy links a newly created article holding the resolution steps as resolution

Verify Checklist Items.evidence: the request asks for 'at least 3 items', so exactly 3 checked items is one valid outcome among several; the count of checked items must exceed 2

Verify Knowledge Article Creation.evidence: kb_number 'KB-001' is a server-assigned record number the request and policy never fix, and the seed numbers articles KB0040001 to KB0040006, so the predicate is dropped and the row anchored by id; the title prefix is tightened to the exact title the request gives

notes:
disagreement: value: the checklist stay's cell: one pass counts items with checked != 1, the other items with checked = 0; chose != 1, the tighter predicate, since it counts any value other than done and the two agree on the seed's values 0 and 1 (resolved on that requirement).
disagreement: value: the new knowledge article's state: one pass tests state = 'published', the other leaves state untested; chose published, since the request requires the article to be linked to the case, the policy makes only published articles linkable, and every article linked to a case in the seed is published (resolved on that requirement).
The passes otherwise agree on every requirement, id, cell and disposition (five checks kept, two repaired); their texts and assumptions differ in wording only.
The policy's knowledge creation clause says a new article is 'drafted' and linked; this is read as writing the article, not as state draft, since the state rule forbids linking an unpublished article.
The case number HRC0000771 is a server-kept record number; the case is identified by hr_case_id 61 instead, which is the row the same number would name (case 60 holds HRC0000770). The case check is split into creation (service, COE, account, group) and closure (status); the notifications check is split into one requirement per recipient.
The acting user, Karen Watkins, holds the admin role, and the policy says an administrator must not perform routine HR case work; the request and every benchmark check expect the work done, so the file specifies the completed work, although a policy-strict agent might halt.
The policy's priority default for new cases is moderate while its enumeration lists medium; the seed uses moderate, so moderate is tested.
Closing the case 'directly' is read as reaching closed_complete; the policy allows no direct move to closed.
Not tested, since neither the request nor the policy fixes them: the case's opened_by (the requester is an administrator, which the policy's description of opened_by does not cover), the article's visibility, the notifications' type and status, and the task's active flag. The policy's case short-description template (Service: , Subject: , Detail: .) is a format rule the benchmark does not test, so it is left out.
